learning_objective: 🎯 Understand how the vast ocean of Ragas is logically organized using the Thaat system, the number of notes (Jati), and the scientific Time Theory of Ragas.

key_vocabulary.definition: A parent scale of 7 notes from which Ragas are derived.
The classification of a Raga based on the number of notes it uses in its ascent (Arohav) and descent (Avaroh).
A Raga Jati that uses exactly 5 notes.
A Raga Jati that uses exactly 6 notes.
A Raga Jati that uses all 7 notes.

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Pt. V.N. Bhatkhande categorized all North Indian Ragas under 10 parent scales (Thaats). A Thaat must have 7 notes in order, but it doesn't need to sound beautiful (unlike a Raga). The 10 Thaats are: Bilawal, Kalyan, Khamaj, Bhairav, Purvi, Marwa, Kafi, Asavari, Bhairavi, and Todi.

A Raga must have a minimum of 5 notes. Depending on notes in Arohav (up) and Avaroh (down), there are 3 main Jatis: Audav (5), Shadav (6), and Sampoorna (7). By combining these (e.g., Audav-Sampoorna: 5 up, 7 down), we get 9 sub-Jatis of Ragas.

main_concepts.concept_title: 🕰️ The Time Theory of Ragas (Samay Chakra)
main_concepts.simple_explanation: In Hindustani music, Ragas are assigned specific times of day based on their dominant notes to maximize their emotional impact. The 24-hour day is divided into two parts: Purvang (12 PM to 12 AM) and Uttarang (12 AM to 12 PM). Ragas are classified into 3 time-categories based on Swaras.

1. Sandhiprakash Ragas (Sunrise/Sunset): Use Komal Re & Dha (e.g., Bhairav). 2. Mid-day/Mid-night Ragas: Use Shuddha Re & Dha (e.g., Kalyan, Bilawal). 3. Late morning/Late night Ragas: Use Komal Ga & Ni (e.g., Kafi, Asavari). The use of Teevra Ma usually shifts a Raga's time to the evening/night.

fun_activity.title: 🔢 Calculate the Jati
fun_activity.instructions: Raga Bhopali uses 5 notes going up (Sa, Re, Ga, Pa, Dha) and 5 notes coming down. What is its Jati? (Answer: Audav-Audav). Raga Yaman uses all 7 notes both ways. What is its Jati? (Answer: Sampoorna-Sampoorna). Knowing the Jati prevents you from playing the wrong forbidden notes!

exam_tips: 📌 Always define Thaat as the 'parent scale' and Raga as the 'child'. A Thaat is only sung as a scale; a Raga is sung with emotion (Rasa).
📌 Sandhiprakash means 'twilight' (dawn and dusk). Remember that these ragas feature Komal Re and Komal Dha.

📌 The Vadi Swara (King note) also dictates time: If Vadi is in the lower half of the scale (Purvang: Sa to Ma), it's sung between 12 PM and 12 AM. If in the upper half (Uttarang: Pa to Taar Sa), it's sung between 12 AM and 12 PM.
quick_recap: ⭐ The 9 sub-Jatis are combinations of the ascent and descent: Audav-Audav, Audav-Shadav, Audav-Sampoorna, Shadav-Audav, etc.
⭐ Teevra Ma (sharp Ma) is called the 'Adhvadarshak Swara' (time-indicator note) because its presence usually signals evening/night ragas, while Shuddha Ma points to morning/day ragas.
⭐ Pt. Bhatkhande's 10 Thaat system is a simplification; South Indian (Carnatic) music uses a much broader 72 Melakarta (parent scale) system.
